postTitle: Geographic Arbitrage: Living Abroad to Save More
topic: Lower living costs work twice: more is saved each year and the pot needed is smaller

caption.instagram:
Same pay, half the living costs. Why could that cut working years by more than half?

Because lower costs work twice. A common starting target for financial independence is a pot of 25 times yearly spending. At €48,000 a year that is €1.2 million; at €24,000 it is €600,000. And from the same €80,000 of pay after tax, the share saved rises from 40% to 70%.

A faster pace toward a closer finish line: starting from zero, at an illustrative 5% a year after inflation, about 22 years of saving becomes about 9.

What decides whether it holds in practice: tax in both countries, the right to live there, healthcare, currency, and whether the move lasts. The 25 times figure is a starting point from US data, not an answer.
